findings.title: enableSqlExpressions is dead/inverted and ignores the feature toggle
findings.body: The helper computes enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions) but then returns false in both branches. As a result FlagSqlExpressions has no effect and the code reads as though it might enable SQL expressions when it never can. If the intent is a hard security disable, return false unconditionally or remove the SQL path; if the intent is toggle-controlled behavior, the current logic is wrong. This leaves a misleading feature-toggle contract for operators and future maintainers.

findings.title: No automated test verifies that SQL expressions are disabled
findings.body: The security fix adds a gate in ReadQuery for QueryTypeSQL but no unit test is included. Without a test asserting that a SQL expression query returns an error both when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled and disabled, a future refactor could accidentally re-enable the SQL expression path and reintroduce the vulnerability.

findings.title: Zero-row SQL result NoData value is immediately overwritten
findings.body: In SQLCommand.Execute, when frame.Rows() == 0 the code sets rsp.Values to mathexp.NoData, but the following unconditional assignment replaces it with mathexp.TableData. Therefore the no-data case is never returned. SQL expressions are currently disabled, but if this code path is ever reached the result type will be wrong for empty results.
